blocks.prompt: 4 If \(z_1 = 2 + 3i\) and \(z_2 = 1 - \alpha\), find the value of \(\alpha\) such that \(\operatorname{Im}(z_1 z_2) = 7\).
blocks.explanation:
A product of two complex numbers with one unknown real number \(\alpha\).
\(\operatorname{Im}(z_1 z_2)\) means the imaginary part of the product (the real number in front of \(i\)).
The book prints \(z_2 = 1 - \alpha\) without \(i\) (see the Book correction below); its answer \(\alpha = -2\) belongs to \(z_2 = 1 - \alpha i\), which we solve, and we also show the printed version.
steps:
Given: \(z_1 = 2 + 3i\), \(z_2 = 1 - \alpha i\) (the intended form; printed \(1 - \alpha\)), \(\alpha\) real, \(\operatorname{Im}(z_1 z_2) = 7\).
To find: \(\alpha\).
Method: Multiply \(z_1 z_2\), write it as (real part) + (imaginary part)\(i\), set the imaginary part equal to 7 and solve.

Multiply \(z_1\) and \(z_2\)
\[z_1 z_2 = (2 + 3i)(1 - \alpha i)\]
\[= 2 - 2\alpha i + 3i - 3\alpha i^2\]
\[= 2 - 2\alpha i + 3i + 3\alpha\]
\[= (2 + 3\alpha) + (3 - 2\alpha)i\]
Why: Multiply every term; \(-3\alpha i^2 = +3\alpha\) is real. Then group the real terms and the \(i\) terms.

Set the imaginary part equal to 7
\[3 - 2\alpha = 7\]
\[-2\alpha = 4\]
\[\alpha = -2\]
Why: The imaginary part is the coefficient of \(i\), here \(3 - 2\alpha\); never include the \(i\) itself.

The printed version, for comparison
\[(2 + 3i)(1 - \alpha)\]
\[= 2(1 - \alpha) + 3(1 - \alpha)i\]
\[3(1 - \alpha) = 7\]
\[\alpha = -\dfrac{4}{3}\]
Why: With \(z_2 = 1 - \alpha\) exactly as printed (a real number), the answer would be \(-\tfrac{4}{3}\), not the key's \(-2\); this shows the \(i\) was dropped in printing.

Check
\[\alpha = -2: \; z_2 = 1 + 2i\]
\[(2 + 3i)(1 + 2i)\]
\[= 2 + 4i + 3i + 6i^2\]
\[= -4 + 7i\]
\[\operatorname{Im} = 7 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The imaginary part of the product is 7, as required.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The question prints \(z_2 = 1 - \alpha\). With a real \(\alpha\) this gives \(\operatorname{Im}(z_1 z_2) = 3(1 - \alpha) = 7\), so \(\alpha = -\frac{4}{3}\), which does not match the answer key's \(\alpha = -2\). The intended number is \(z_2 = 1 - \alpha i\); then \(\operatorname{Im}(z_1 z_2) = 3 - 2\alpha = 7\) gives \(\alpha = -2\).
